summary: 1964 Washington DNR wooden lookout on private timberland in Pierce County; access needs a permit; restored with FFLA volunteers in 2017.

facts.design: 14 by 14 foot live-in flattop cab with catwalk on a wooden DNR tower

access.note: Private timberland. Vehicle access needs an annual permit, and motorized access to the summit is not allowed.

visit.trail_note: Hike-in route of 21 miles round trip with about 2,500 feet of gain (TrailChick). Permits needed. Copper Creek Hut is about 6 miles away.

events.note: Built by the Washington DNR; the Forest Lookouts page cites a replacement tower erected in 1962-64
Grant from the Chuck Butler Memorial Fund for the restoration. The report gives no amount.
Forest Fire Lookout Association members helped restore the tower; work parties permitted by the landowner

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Four sources give 1964 as the build year. The Forest Lookouts page describes a replacement tower erected in 1962-64, which is consistent with a 1964 completion.
Kept 6.1 m (20 feet). Firelookout.com, Will Hite and TrailChick give 20 feet. The Register alone gives 30 feet.

sources.title: Eastern Washington 2017 Chapter Report
sources.publisher: Forest Fire Lookout Association, Eastern Washington Chapter

notes_for_editor: Record checks out: location (46.833973, -122.017157) and elevation 1464.3 m match NHLR (4,804 ft / 1,464 m), and the agency and 1964 build year agree, so no corrections. Elevation conflicts, left out of facts: NHLR 4,804 ft; firelookout.com 4930 ft; Will Hite 4930 or 4,877 ft; TrailChick 4,877 ft. Height conflicts: Register says 30 ft, others 20 ft; kept 6.1 m. Owner names conflict: the Register names Plum Creek Timber Co. and Champion International; Will Hite and TrailChick say Kapowsin Tree Farm, with permits via Hancock Forest Management; TrailChick's 2017 note names Manke Lumber Company as landowner. Left unresolved. Route length conflicts: TrailChick gives 21 miles round trip; Will Hite gives 'More than 10, less than 15' with 'Good Gravel Roads' to the start. The access level 'permission' is editorial, from the permit requirement in Will Hite and TrailChick. The 2017 report describes help with restoration and the grant but not completion; nothing newer found. TrailChick updated May 2026 but its photos are from a 2018 visit. Staffing is not in any source, so it is left out. The firelookout.com photo (credit Mike Kretzler) was not licence-checked; no photos added.
